title: Select the local OSC listening interface
problem: Linux Show Player derives one local address from the routing table and binds its OSC listener there, so a user with multiple networks cannot receive show-control traffic on another interface.
reproduce: Expose two IPv4 interfaces in the OSC settings and request a specific bind address; the pinned baseline has no selector and OscServer cannot accept a bind-address argument.
acceptance: The settings list all current IPv4 interfaces plus an all-interfaces option, retain a saved address that is temporarily unavailable, pass the selection to the OSC listener, and restart the listener when it changes.
repair: Add a local-address combo box, persist bindAddress independently from the remote OSC hostname, preserve the previous auto-selected address for legacy configurations, and restart the UDP listener on changes.

selection.reason: A two-day-old external report gives an exact multi-network failure on current develop; the focused UI and server tests reproduce it without hardware and the reporter can immediately validate routing on Debian.

verification.limitations: BCL exercises the actual Qt settings widget and OSC server wiring with deterministic interface and UDP-server doubles. A live multi-interface Debian installation remains owner-validated.
verification.ownerCheck: Open OSC settings on the Debian machine with both networks connected, select the control-network address, apply settings, send an OSC message to that IP and input port, and confirm Linux Show Player receives it; repeat after restarting the application.
